title: 2017 AMC 10B Problem 10
statement: The lines with equations \(ax-2y=c\) and \(2x+by=-c\) are perpendicular and intersect at \((1, -5).\) What is \(c?\)

solutions.text:
The first equation can be rewritten as \(y=\dfrac a2x-\dfrac c2,\) and the second as \(y=-\dfrac2b x-\dfrac cb.\) Because the lines are perpendicular, their slopes multiply to \(-1,\) so \(a=b.\)

Substituting \((x,y)=(1,-5)\) into the two original equations gives \(a+10=c\) and \(2-5a=-c.\) Adding these equations yields \(12-4a=0,\) so \(a=3\) and \(c=13.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E .
hints: Rewrite both lines in slope-intercept form
Perpendicular slopes and the point \((1,-5)\) determine the parameters
